definitionBean.title: Neutralization Reaction
definitionBean.definition: When an acid and a base react with each other, they neutralize each other's effect to form salt and water. This process is called a 'neutralization reaction'.
definitionBean.explanation: In this reaction, the $\text{H}^+$ ion of the acid and the $\text{OH}^-$ ion of the base combine to form water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$). This is an exothermic reaction in which energy is released.
importantPoints: Neutral products (salt and water) are formed
Heat is produced in the reaction

definitionBean.title: Important Salts
definitionBean.definition: Various useful chemicals such as baking soda, washing soda, bleaching powder, and plaster of Paris are obtained from common salt ($\text{NaCl}$).
definitionBean.explanation: These salts are widely used in our daily life, industries, and the medical field.

parts.statement: What is a neutralization reaction? Give an example.
parts.correct_answer: Formation of salt and water from the combination of an acid and a base is neutralization.
parts.explanation: When an acid and a base react together to form salt and water, it is called a neutralization reaction. Example: $\text{NaOH} + \text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$.

parts.statement: Write the chemical names and formulas of baking soda and plaster of Paris.
parts.explanation: Baking Soda: Sodium hydrogen carbonate ($\text{NaHCO}_3$); Plaster of Paris: Calcium sulfate hemihydrate ($\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O}$).
